The money went as outsized commissions to the agent Zwi Skornicki under consulting agreements, and he passed it on. Keppel took a deferred prosecution agreement in December 2017, its American subsidiary pleaded guilty, and Skornicki pleaded guilty in 2019. Fines across three countries came to 422 million dollars, and in December 2022 Brazil's comptroller and attorney-general settled for a further 1.22 billion reais.
inside: A rig builder's agent paid Petrobras officials and the governing party, and the state oil company awarded it thirteen rig and platform contracts.
cite: US Department of Justice, deferred prosecution agreement and criminal information against Keppel Offshore & Marine, Eastern District of New York, 22 December 2017, and the information and plea agreement against Zwi Skornicki of 25 June 2019, as recorded by the Stanford Law School Foreign Corrupt Practices Act Clearinghouse; and the Acordos de Leniencia dataset of Brazil's Portal da Transparencia, process 00190.111425/2017-18, for the agreement of 19 December 2022 worth R$1,223,657,710.19

n: SBM Offshore's commissions reached Petrobras officials over vessel work
rank: Petrobras officials
d: SBM Offshore, a Dutch company that builds and leases floating oil production vessels, paid commissions to an intermediary on projects Petrobras awarded it, knowing the intermediary would pass part of the money to officials of Brazil's state oil company. The US Justice Department said the scheme ran from at least 1996 to 2012 and that SBM paid more than 180 million dollars in commissions across Brazil, Angola, Equatorial Guinea, Kazakhstan and Iraq; its American subsidiary took at least 13.2 million dollars from Petrobras work. The company kept records of the scheme in a safe in its Monaco office. It paid a 238 million dollar criminal penalty in the United States in November 2017, and in July 2018 settled with Brazil's comptroller, its attorney-general and Petrobras for 549 million reais.
inside: A vessel contractor's commissions to an intermediary reached Petrobras officials, and the state oil company kept awarding it production-vessel projects.
cite: US Department of Justice, criminal information against SBM Offshore N.V., Southern District of Texas, 30 November 2017, on the commissions paid to Intermediary 1 for Petrobras projects and the records kept in Monaco; SBM Offshore annual report for 2018, compliance reporting section, on the leniency agreement of 26 July 2018 with the CGU, the AGU and Petrobras; and the Acordos de Leniencia dataset of Brazil's Portal da Transparencia, process 00190.007023/2015-40

n: Jurong's shipyards settled claims of paying officials over Petrobras work
org_label: Seatrium, Jurong Shipyard and Estaleiro Jurong Aracruz
rank: Brazilian public officials in Petrobras contracting
d: Seatrium and Jurong Shipyard, both based in Singapore, and the Brazilian yard Estaleiro Jurong Aracruz settled claims that they paid improper benefits to Brazilian public officials in connection with contracts with Petrobras, the state oil company, between 2007 and 2014. Brazil's comptroller and attorney-general announced the agreement on 30 July 2025, under the Clean Company Act, for 728,309,320.80 reais payable to the state and to Petrobras. The announcement does not name the officials who were paid or the individual contracts, so what is on the record is the settlement's own account of the conduct rather than a court's finding. Seatrium was formed from the merger of Sembcorp Marine with the offshore and marine arm of Keppel, whose own Petrobras bribery is a separate case.
inside: Shipyards settled claims that their payments reached Brazilian officials in the state oil company's contracting, over work awarded between 2007 and 2014.
cite: Advocacia-Geral da Uniao and Controladoria-Geral da Uniao, joint announcement of the leniency agreement with Seatrium Limited, Jurong Shipyard Pte. Ltd. and Estaleiro Jurong Aracruz, 30 July 2025, which gives the period, the conduct and the figure and states that no specific official or contract is identified; and the Acordos de Leniencia dataset of Brazil's Portal da Transparencia, process 00190.109025/2019-04

n: Rolls-Royce's intermediaries paid Petrobras officials for turbine work
rank: Petrobras officials
d: Rolls-Royce, the British engineering group, won supply contracts from Brazil's state oil company Petrobras after intermediaries it hired paid officials there. The US Justice Department says Rolls-Royce used intermediaries to pay about 9.3 million dollars to officials of a state-owned petroleum corporation that awarded it multiple contracts, and that the Brazilian conspiracy ran from 2005 to 2008; of those commissions, at least 1.6 million dollars reached a Brazilian official. The work was gas turbines supplied to the company. Brazil's comptroller-general puts the acts in 2003, 2004 and 2005. Federal prosecutors settled on 13 January 2017 for 81,183,700 reais paid straight to Petrobras: the profit on six contracts, the commissions to intermediaries, and a fine under the improbity law equal to those commissions. The comptroller-general and the attorney-general put the Brazilian total at 27,825,636.37 dollars on 25 October 2021, of which 2,215,636.37 was new money, the rest already paid.
inside: Rolls-Royce's hired intermediaries paid Petrobras officials, and the state oil company awarded it gas turbine contracts.
cite: US Department of Justice, 'Rolls-Royce plc Agrees to Pay $170 Million Criminal Penalty', 17 January 2017, for the 9.3 million dollar figure and the conduct; Miller & Chevalier FCPA Winter Review 2017 for the 2005-2008 Brazilian conspiracy and the 1.6 million dollars reaching an official; Cleary Gottlieb client alert, 19 January 2017, for the gas turbine contracts; Ministério Público Federal, Procuradoria da República no Paraná, 'MPF firma acordo de leniência com Rolls-Royce', on the agreement of 13 January 2017; Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU assinam acordo de leniência com a Rolls-Royce PLC', 25 October 2021; Saud Advogados, 2021, for the split of that total

n: Viken's broker money paid Transpetro's president over tanker charters
rank: President of Transpetro
d: Transpetro is the shipping arm of Brazil's state oil company Petrobras. Federal prosecutors charged in 2019 that its then president, Sérgio Machado, took money to steer tanker charters: 11.9 million reais for himself and for members of the MDB party to secure a contract for the shipping firm Noroil between February and August 2010, and about 1.6 million reais over a Suezmax tanker for Viken Hull in 2011 and 2012. Three Norwegian companies of the Viken group paid a brokerage commission that a third party used to fund the benefit to Machado. They say their representatives did not know of or authorise the payments, but accepted strict liability and settled with the comptroller-general and the attorney-general's office on 13 June 2024 for about 152 million reais, paid to Transpetro International BV and the federal government.
inside: Shipowners' commission money reached the president of Petrobras's shipping arm, who steered tanker charters to the firms that paid.
cite: Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU assinam acordo de leniência com empresas norueguesas', 13 June 2024, which names PAR 00190.110786/2018-10, and the CGU's Relatório Final in process 00190.106328/2019-67; Ministério Público Federal Paraná task force denúncia against José Sérgio de Oliveira Machado and Paulo César Chafic Haddad of April 2019, as reported by Gazeta do Povo and O Povo, 3 July 2019. What became of that criminal case is not established here

n: Hypermarcas director's payments aimed at senators over a drug tax bill
rank: MDB senators, not proven
d: Hypermarcas, now Hypera, is a large Brazilian drugmaker. Its former director of institutional relations, Nelson José de Mello, told prosecutors in a plea deal that he signed fictitious contracts with firms named by the lobbyist Milton Lyra to pass money to MDB senators so they would favour the company in the Senate; the police said the return was help with a 2014 and 2015 bill on drug industry tax breaks. Mello said he did not know exactly who the beneficiaries were, and that the payments were made without the knowledge of the company's owner. The police indicted senators Renan Calheiros and Eduardo Braga and the former senator Romero Jucá in September 2024, but the prosecutor-general found no evidence the money reached them and Justice Edson Fachin closed the inquiry in October 2024. Jucá's lawyers rejected the indictment. The company settled with the comptroller-general and the attorney-general on 31 May 2022 for 110,882,122.19 reais.
inside: A drugmaker's director paid a lobbyist to reach senators over a tax bill; prosecutors found no proof the money got to them.
cite: Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU celebram acordo de leniência de R$ 110 milhões com empresas relacionadas ao grupo Hypera S.A.', 31 May 2022; InfoMoney, 29 October 2024, on Justice Edson Fachin closing the inquiry and the prosecutor-general's reasoning; Diário do Poder, on the Federal Police final report and Romero Jucá's response; Consultor Jurídico, 4 June 2019, on the request to cancel Mello's plea deal

n: Qualicorp paid to avoid tax assessments as auditors took money
rank: Receita Federal tax inspectors
d: Qualicorp is a Brazilian broker of collective health plans. Two Federal Police operations of 2020 lie behind its settlement. In Paralelo 23, in July 2020, its founder José Seripieri Filho was held over 5 million reais the police say he passed to José Serra's 2014 Senate campaign through a structure that hid the transfers; a judge revoked the temporary arrest days later. Triuno, in October 2020, was worked up with the federal revenue service and prosecutors: three federal tax inspectors and a state inspector are suspected of taking money to cut companies' tax bills or speed up refunds, and the case file says Qualicorp made use of the scheme while Seripieri ran it. The comptroller-general and the attorney-general settled on 17 March 2025 for 44,485,434.29 reais over undue payments in 2013 and 2014 made to avoid tax assessments. Qualicorp approached them in 2021 and gave evidence from an internal committee and a former director.
inside: A health-plan broker paid to avoid federal tax assessments; investigators suspect tax inspectors took money to cut the bills of companies that paid.
cite: Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU Assinam Acordo de Leniencia com a Qualicorp', 17 March 2025, for the agreement, the years and the two operations; Policia Federal account of Operação Triuno as reported by Seu Dinheiro, 22 October 2020; O Bastidor on the inspectors arrested and what they are suspected of; Revista redalyc article quoting the investigation file on Qualicorp's use of the scheme; Correio Braziliense, 24 July 2020, on the arrest in Paralelo 23 and its revocation

n: A tourism group settled over payments reaching a tax appeals judge
org_label: Mar Holding and Operadora e Agência de Viagens TUR
rank: CARF councillor; a Receita Federal auditor
d: Brazil's CARF is the appeals council inside the finance ministry that decides whether tax assessments stand. On 28 December 2022 the comptroller-general and the attorney-general settled with Mar Holding Participações and the tour operator Operadora e Agência de Viagens TUR for 74,376,821.93 reais, over payments to public officials through third parties between 2013 and 2015 to win favour in tax proceedings. A 2024 CGU note on the agreement's own history of the acts says TUR signed simulated legal-services contracts with a law office worth about 32 million reais, that a further 5.2 million reais went to five companies the office named and was drawn in cash and handed to the CARF councillor Fernando Lobo D'Eça, and that CARF then granted TUR's appeal. The note treats this as the company's account rather than as proven and recommends no action against the group. The investigation began from the plea deal of Guilherme Paulus of the group; he and five others were later charged over payments to get tax refunds released. In June 2026 the CGU fined four of the firms that carried the money 5.1 million reais in all.
inside: A tourism group settled over payments that, by its own account, reached the tax appeals councillor who then granted its appeal.
cite: Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU celebram acordo de leniência de R$ 74,3 milhões com empresas do setor de turismo', 28 December 2022, for the agreement, the years and the conduct, which it attributes to Operação Descarte and which names neither CARF nor any individual; CGU Nota Técnica 1555/2024 on the agreement's histórico de atos lesivos, for the contracts, the cash, the named councillor and the auditor, all of which it hedges; CGU, 'CGU sanciona empresas por corrupção no CARF', 26 June 2026, for the four companies fined and the Operação Checkout scheme

n: Two meat companies paid the farm ministry's inspectors in Tocantins
rank: Federal agricultural inspectors, Ministry of Agriculture
d: Brazil's agriculture ministry posts federal agricultural inspectors who certify meat plants, and two companies have settled claims of paying them in Tocantins. Minerva, a Brazilian beef processor, agreed on 9 May 2025 to pay 22,040,373.16 reais over payments to the ministry's inspectors at Araguaína, in acts the comptroller-general dates to before 2018 and which two Federal Police operations, Lucas and Vegas, investigated across more than a dozen food companies. Minerva says the sum is only the Clean Company Act fine and that no loss to the treasury or gain to the company was found. Bonasa Alimentos, an animal-protein producer based in the Federal District, settled on 26 January 2026 for 631,799.74 reais over the same inspection service and the same two operations, in acts dated 2013 to 2017; the comptroller-general names no town for it. Bonasa came to the comptroller-general of its own accord. Both companies handed over information that, the comptroller-general says, let the authorities proceed against the officials.
inside: Two meat companies paid the agriculture ministry's inspectors in Tocantins, the officials who certify their plants' meat as fit.
cite: Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU assinam acordo de leniência com empresa de processamento de alimentos', 9 May 2025, which carries the Minerva agreement, the inspectors at Araguaína, Operações Lucas and Vegas and the dating to before 2018; Finance News, 9 May 2025, for Minerva's own statement and the exact figure; Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU assinam acordo de leniência com empresa do setor de alimentos do DF', on the Bonasa agreement of 26 January 2026, for the figure, the acts of 2013 to 2017, Tocantins and the two operations; the Bonasa agreement's own clause 2.1.1 on gov.br, for the company coming forward of its own accord

n: A meat plant at Santa Fé de Goiás paid the inspectors who certify it
rank: Federal agricultural inspectors, Ministry of Agriculture
d: Prima Foods runs a meat plant at Santa Fé de Goiás, a small town in western Goiás. Undue advantages were paid there to the agriculture ministry's federal agricultural inspectors, the officials who certify meat plants, to ease or cover up sanitary and administrative irregularities. The conduct ran from 2012 to 2019 and came out in a Federal Police operation, Conduta de Risco II. On 26 January 2026 Prima Foods and JBJ Agropecuária settled with the comptroller-general and the attorney-general for 31,156,767.70 reais in three yearly instalments: 30,508,766.99 from Prima Foods and 648,000.70 from JBJ. The two signed one agreement because Prima Foods belongs to and is controlled by the JBJ group, which benefited directly from the conduct. Clause 8.1.1 sets off whatever the companies pay under an earlier agreement with federal prosecutors, so less than the headline sum reaches the federal government. The companies gave information and documents that let the authorities proceed against the officials involved.
inside: A meat group paid the agriculture ministry's inspectors in Goiás to ease or cover up sanitary problems at its plant.
cite: Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU assinam acordo de leniência com empresas produtoras de proteína animal', on the agreement of 26 January 2026, for the signing date, the figure and the years in Goiás; the signed agreement on gov.br, clauses 8.1, 8.1.1 and 8.2, for the set-off against the prosecutors' agreement and the three yearly instalments, and its Anexo III for the split between the two companies; Regionalzão, 10 February 2026, for Operação Conduta de Risco II and the Prima Foods unit at Santa Fé de Goiás; Metrópoles, 'JBJ Agropecuária e Prima Foods pagam R$ 31 milhões por corromper fiscais', for the payments being made to ease or cover up sanitary and administrative irregularities; Saud Advogados' review of the CGU's 2026 agreements for the group relationship

n: Bilfinger confessed to corruption in the Brazilian Navy's nuclear programme
rank: Brazilian Navy; its nuclear programme
d: Bilfinger Maschinenbau, an engineering partnership constituted under Austrian law and seated at Linz, confessed to corruption in its dealings with the Brazilian Navy. It supplied material for the Navy's nuclear programme, which is developing a nuclear-powered submarine and the fuel cycle behind it. The attorney-general's office dates those supply contracts to between 2012 and 2017; the agreement itself records that the company stopped making improper payments to public agents on 5 December 2013. The company approached Brazil's comptroller-general after an independent audit it commissioned confirmed irregularities in its administrative contracts; by then the comptroller-general had opened proceedings against it, in March 2015, and negotiations ran from that June to August 2017. The agreement of 14 August 2017, the second ever signed under the Clean Company Act, came to 2,658,169.72 euros: 2,248,290.33 in compensation, 355,235.62 as the Clean Company Act fine and 54,643.77 under the improbity law. In December 2021 the comptroller-general certified that every obligation had been met, the first company so certified. Bilfinger would not discuss details, citing the confidentiality the law imposes.
inside: An engineering firm admitted paying inside the Brazilian Navy over contracts to supply its nuclear submarine programme.
cite: Advocacia-Geral da União statement of 14 August 2017, carried by DefesaNet, for the Navy, the nuclear programme supply contracts of 2012 to 2017, the company's own audit and its refusal to discuss details; the signed agreement on gov.br, clauses 1.2, 2.1.2, 2.1.3, 6.1.1, 6.1.2 and 8.3, for the Austrian constitution and Linz seat, the payments ceasing on 5 December 2013, the PAR opened on 27 March 2015, the negotiations and the three parts of the sum - the agreement names no public body, the conduct being in annexes that are not published; Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU atesta cumprimento de acordo de leniência pela empresa Bilfinger Maschinenbau', December 2021; Revista Direito e Justiça, 'Acordos de leniência da Lei Anticorrupção', for its being the second such agreement

n: Desenvix paid for the release of north-eastern development loans
rank: Public agents of Banco do Nordeste
d: The Fundo Constitucional de Financiamento do Nordeste, or FNE, is a federal fund that lends to businesses in Brazil's north-east, and Banco do Nordeste, a state-owned development bank in Fortaleza, administers it. Desenvix, the energy arm of the builder Engevix, paid bribes connected with FNE money between 2011 and 2014. The Norwegian state power company Statkraft took control of Desenvix in July 2015, investigated it and reported what it found to the Brazilian authorities in 2016; it says the payments were made to speed up approvals by public bodies. Reporting on a later comptroller-general inquiry says the money went to public agents of Banco do Nordeste in return for releasing the bank's funds for the company's projects. On 15 October 2021 the renamed Statkraft Energias Renováveis and three of its wind companies settled for 18.01 million reais, of which 2,404,359.30 is restitution of money paid as bribes.
inside: An energy company's money reached officials of the state development bank that decides who gets north-eastern development loans.
cite: Controladoria-Geral da União and Advocacia-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU assinam acordo de leniência com Statkraft Energias Renováveis S.A.', 15 October 2021, for the four companies, the years, the FNE and the breakdown of the 18.01 million reais, none of which names a bank or an official; Statkraft, 'Agreement in Brazil', 16 October 2021, for the acquisition, its own investigation and the payments to speed up public approvals; Metrópoles, 'CGU de Lula quer investigar caso que citou propina a líder do governo', for the CGU's Investigação Preliminar Sumária opened after the agreement and the payments to public agents of Banco do Nordeste - the only source for that body, which is why the record is coded probable; Banco do Nordeste's own profile report for its seat in Fortaleza and its administration of the FNE

n: Neoway's rigged tenders ran through Santa Catarina's state bodies
rank: Santa Catarina state bodies, above all the health secretariat
d: Neoway, a data and technology company from Santa Catarina, settled with Brazil's comptroller-general and attorney-general on 4 December 2023 over acts against the public administration between 2006 and 2019. Operation Alcatraz, begun in 2017 by the Federal Police and the revenue service, investigated rigged tenders in the state, overpriced goods and services bought by the state government, information technology above all, the diversion of state and federal money, bribes to public agents and money laundering. What it found, with an examination of tenders and contracts by the state audit prosecutors, pointed to irregularities in contracts signed between 2006 and 2018 by several state secretariats, above all the health secretariat, with strong indications of losses to the national health service. A second operation, Hemorragia, followed. The state-level agreement Neoway signed in February 2022 measured the damage across 17 of its contracts with six bodies and entities of the state executive. The agreement came to 27,178,868.56 reais, of which Neoway still owed the 4,716,107.57 fine, two agreements in 2022 with federal prosecutors and the state comptroller having covered the rest.
inside: A technology company's money reached public agents in Santa Catarina's state bodies, which awarded and extended its contracts.
cite: Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU assinam acordo de leniência com Neoway Tecnologia Integrada', on the agreement of 4 December 2023, and its fuller version at Agência Gov, for the figures, the years, what Operations Alcatraz and Hemorragia found, the state secretariats and the health secretariat, and the two earlier agreements; the signed agreement on gov.br, whose clause 5.3 has the company admitting payment of undue advantage to public agents; Migalhas, 17 February 2022, for the 17 contracts with six bodies and entities of the state executive measured in the Santa Catarina agreement; Istoé Dinheiro, 5 December 2023, on the rigging and the improper extensions. The Receita Federal dates Alcatraz to 2019 and Hemorragia to 2021, where the CGU has Alcatraz beginning in 2017

n: A machinery dealer paid over sales under Banco do Brasil rural credit
rank: A Banco do Brasil rural credit programme
d: Banco do Brasil, the state-controlled bank, runs rural credit programmes that finance farmers' purchases of equipment. Between 2018 and 2021 Mauro Luvizoto Máquinas, a machinery dealer, paid undue advantages in connection with the intermediation of agricultural machinery sales under one of those programmes. The comptroller-general and the attorney-general settled with it in December 2023 for 196,179.57 reais - 65,458.52 as the fine and 130,721.05 given up as the advantage obtained - the first leniency agreement either had signed with a small company; the secretary for private integrity said the case showed such agreements can settle isolated non-compliance as well as large schemes. The company also has to put integrity measures in place. The comptroller-general's announcement does not say who received the payments, and does not name the company either, describing it only as a dealer in agricultural machinery and equipment; the name and the process number come from the public register of agreements, which records this one as fulfilled.
inside: A machinery dealer paid undue advantages over sales financed by a state bank's rural credit programme; who received them is not named.
cite: Controladoria-Geral da União release of December 2023 as carried by Agência Gov, 'CGU e AGU assinam acordo de leniência pela 1ª vez com empresa de pequeno porte', for the years, the Banco do Brasil rural credit programme, the figure and the quotation from the secretary for private integrity; the Acordos de Leniência dataset of Brazil's Portal da Transparência, process 00190.104707/2022-18, for the agreement being recorded as fulfilled

n: Foster Wheeler got inside help from a Petrobras manager for UFN-IV
rank: A manager in Petrobras's engineering department
d: Petrobras, Brazil's state oil company, put out to tender the design of a gas-to-chemicals complex it called UFN-IV. Foster Wheeler Energy, the British engineering business later bought by Amec and then by John Wood Group, won it by getting inside the company that was choosing. The US Justice Department says it offered and paid bribes to decision-makers at Petrobras through intermediaries including an Italian agent, and that it won the contract by obtaining confidential documents, inside information and secret assistance from a manager in Petrobras's engineering department. The Securities and Exchange Commission puts the bribes at about 1.1 million dollars. On 25 June 2021 the comptroller-general, the attorney-general and federal prosecutors settled for 86,196,063.32 reais, of which 67,273,820.43 went back to Petrobras and the rest was fines. That was Brazil's part of one coordinated resolution: the Securities and Exchange Commission put the whole of it, across the American, British and Brazilian authorities, at more than 43 million dollars for this scheme.
inside: An engineering company paid for confidential documents and secret help from a manager inside Petrobras, and won the design contract he helped decide.
cite: US Securities and Exchange Commission, 'SEC Charges Amec Foster Wheeler Limited With FCPA Violations Related To Brazilian Bribery Scheme', 25 June 2021, for the UFN-IV contract, the 1.1 million dollars, and the coordinated resolution of more than 43 million dollars, which that order says covers the American, British and Brazilian authorities together; the US Department of Justice's criminal information, for the bribes to decision-makers at Petrobras, the Italian agent, and the confidential documents, inside information and secret assistance from a manager in Petrobras's engineering department; Controladoria-Geral da União and Advocacia-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU celebram acordo de leniência de R$ 86 milhões com empresas por ilícitos em projeto com a Petrobras', 25 June 2021, for the Brazilian figures and the share returned to Petrobras

n: Stericycle paid officials at the health bodies holding its waste contracts
rank: Officials of institutions of the SUS, the national health service
d: Stericycle, an American medical-waste company, held hospital waste contracts through Brazilian subsidiaries with bodies and entities of Brazil's national health service, the SUS, and paid officials there. The US Justice Department and Securities and Exchange Commission found that across Brazil, Mexico and Argentina its staff made hundreds of payments, usually in cash and worked out as a percentage of what the government customers owed the company, and that it kept spreadsheets of which customers had been paid, under code words including 'CP' for commission payment. Brazil's comptroller-general and attorney-general settled on 20 April 2022 for 109,698,073.80 reais, about 65 million of it compensation, 41 million the Clean Company Act fine and 2,853,015.49 the improbity fine, with six group companies signing. Their announcement gives no years for the conduct, which the group found in its own investigation and reported to the comptroller-general in 2018. The American penalties and the credits between the two countries are in the three-country record. Stericycle served a two-year compliance monitorship, and in April 2025 the American charges were dismissed with prejudice seven months early, the prosecutors saying it had fully complied.
inside: A waste company paid officials at the national health service bodies that held its hospital waste contracts and owed it the money its payments were reckoned against.
cite: Advocacia-Geral da União and Controladoria-Geral da União, 'CGU e AGU celebram acordo de leniência de R$ 109 milhões com empresas por ilícitos na coleta de lixo hospitalar em unidades de saúde', 20 April 2022, for the figure, the six companies, the hospital waste contracts with bodies and entities of the SUS and the improbity fine - that release gives no years; Saud Advogados' English note on the same announcement for the split of the Brazilian sum; Maeda, Ayres & Sarubbi, on the group's own internal investigation and its self-report to the CGU in 2018; Willkie Compliance Concourse, 22 April 2022, on the US Justice Department's account of the spreadsheets naming the government customers paid and the code words, and its April 2025 note on the motion to dismiss; Morrison Foerster and Miller & Chevalier, on the dismissal with prejudice in April 2025 and the certification that preceded it; Waste Management's Form 10-Q for 2025, for its acquisition of Stericycle in November 2024 and the dismissal
